Wordfish: positions from word counts

Source: R/svt.R
wrdfsh.Rd

The Poisson scaling model of Slapin and Proksch (2008), \(y_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\exp(\psi_i + \alpha_j + \beta_j \omega_i))\), for documents (judgments, briefs, platforms) by their word counts: alternating Newton steps on the document positions \(\omega\) (standardised after each sweep, the word parameters adjusted to keep the linear predictor) and on the word parameters, from normal starts (seed 42, as set.seed() takes it), until the positions change by a relative tol. The sign of the scale is arbitrary.

Usage

wrdfsh(dtm, maxit = 100, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

dtm

A document-by-term matrix of counts.

maxit

The most sweeps.

tol

The convergence tolerance.

Value

A list of class wrdfsh: pos (\(\omega\)), beta, alpha, psi, loglik and iter.

References

Slapin, J. B. and Proksch, S.-O. (2008). A scaling model for estimating time-series party positions from texts. American Journal of Political Science, 52(3), 705-722. doi:10.1111/j.1540-5907.2008.00338.x

See also

Other scaling: amscal(), anchv(), anomin(), bamscl(), bbscal(), bmdsf(), bunfld(), cjrirt(), cmdsf(), cutlns(), dblctr(), dwnom(), dynirt(), indscl(), ipsrec(), irtem(), irtlik(), irtpst(), mdsfit(), mlsmu(), nmdsf(), nombt(), nomll(), nompr(), nomutl(), nrmvec(), optcls(), ordirt(), ordocl(), procrs(), scboot(), smacf(), smunf(), unfstr(), votagr()

Examples

set.seed(1)
wrdfsh(matrix(rpois(600, 5), 20), maxit = 20)$pos
#>  [1]  1.15570659  0.25111445  0.01650556 -1.49106129  0.13088144 -1.07365520
#>  [7]  1.05617759 -0.83530154 -0.99936159  0.25353260 -0.31732379 -1.84826884
#> [13] -0.20769336  1.06437931  1.98755859  0.68871590  0.01462927 -0.99868738
#> [19]  1.10180015  0.05035155
